kai: Heads-up — we started seeing a cluster of OOMs on long-context workloads this morning. p95 memory spikes on a few workers coincided with increased KV page reads. attaching notes and a tiny repro trace below.

maria: ugh, timeline? is this isolated to a model or global?

kai: Started ~08:12 UTC, affects model variants with >8k tokens active sessions (mostly v2-large-context). Not all hosts; looks correlated with very long conversations + rapid turn-taking (many short turns => repeated cache promos).

dave: any indication of read amplification vs true allocation growth?

kai: profile says amplification. snapshot from perf collector:
```text
kv_page_reads_total: 4.2k -> 18.7k (5x)
kv_pages_read_bytes: 1.9GB -> 6.8GB
kv_reuse_hit_ratio: 0.12
host_free_memory: 12GB -> 2.1GB (spike period)
concurrent_batches: 48 -> 96
```

kai: Repro: when many sessions append small messages, the runtime prefetcher scans adjacent pages and causes repeated page loads because pages are evicted between requests (fragmentation + small slab churn). repeats amplify reads and memory working set spikes.

anna: Can we short-circuit prefetch in long-session mode? Maybe a dynamic prefetch cap based on kv_reuse_hit_ratio.

maria: +1. Also batching heuristics: increasing concurrent_batches during bursts makes KV pressure worse. We should cap batches when host_free_memory < threshold.

kai: Proposed mitigations:
- short term: rollout a runtime flag to disable aggressive prefetch (prefetch_depth=1) and cap concurrent_batches to 32 for canary nodes
- medium: change eviction scoring to prefer contiguous prefix preservation (favor hot prefixes) to reduce re-read amplification
- long term: implement slab compaction + shard-level per-prefix reservation and soft-delta eviction to avoid oscillation
- fallback: if host_free_memory < 3GB, degrade to a short-context model variant (same model family) with explicit "x-rw-kv-shortened: 1" header to callers

dave: I can pick the prefetch flag and batch cap tomorrow. low-risk.

anna: I can prototype an eviction score tweak: score = recency * (1 - frag_penalty) - size*0.1, where frag_penalty is high if page has many small allocations. that should prioritize coalesced pages.

infra-bot: query suggestion: `sum(rate(kv_page_reads_total[5m])) by (host)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(kv_pages_read_bytes[5m])) by (le, host))` — watch for hosts with >200 pages/min and >2GB read/min.

ops-bot: creating incident for visibility and linking runbook: INC-2330-KV-READ-AMP.

kai: Rollout plan:
1) Patch runtime with prefetch_depth flag + batch cap. unit tests + local perf harness.
2) Canary deploy to 5 hosts in us-west for 30m. Metrics to watch: kv_reuse_hit_ratio, kv_page_reads_total, host_free_memory, p95 latency, tokens/s.
3) If stable, ramp to 25% and enable eviction-score experiment on separate canary lane.
4) If ramp looks good, full rollout with opt-in for private clusters.

maria: add alert: kv_reuse_hit_ratio < 0.2 for 10m AND kv_page_reads_total > baseline*3 -> auto-reduce concurrent batches by 25% on impacted hosts.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2330002000 UTC to group: eng-runtime-canary-1.

kai: I'll open the PR with the flag and the perf harness results. leaving notes in the incident. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — ping when PR is up and i'll wire the alert. :eyes:

ops-bot: incident INC-2330-KV-READ-AMP created and paged on-call.
